text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Statistical error which made Finland's budget deficit in 1996 larger than initially reported does not threated Finland's membership in economic monetary union. Decisions will based on 1997 figure, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says.

- Finnish and foreign investors should have equal place in purchasing stocks; Finnish investors should also be allowed to function anonymously or foreign investors' names should be revealed, working group at the Finance Ministry plans. @
- Small group of Finnish forest owners started hunger strike in western Finland in protest at environment ministry's Natura-2000 programme.
- Foreign Ministers of Finland and Latvia agreed on Monday to end visa requirements between both countries in early autumn.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish forestry group UPM Kymmene was listed as the fourth biggest forest company in the world, an international comparison of Fortune Magazine shows.
- Russian markets are biggest for Finnish food exports, making up one-third of total five billion markka trade in 1996.
- Finnish farmers expect grain crop to be larger than last year.
AAMULEHTI
- Natura-2000 programme will undergo changes, Environment Minister Pekka Haavisto says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Common rules for health-product marketing should be created in EU countries; it would harmonise and clarify the legislation, foodstuffs administration authorities say.
- More lightning in July than ever before, Meteorogical Institute says.
DEMARI
- Low-income workers should be supported and a minimum salary requirement included in the pay deal agreement, says Ilkka Joenpelto, chairman of the Union of Technical Employees in Finland.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Helsinki underground celebrates 15th anniversary; has become the most popular means of public transport.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
